Tangent-space active-set LP polish with HiGHS plus dual/stress-guided hole surgery to change contact topology.
direction: Build a fast, correctly budgeted tangent-space active-set LP/SQP polish and use its multipliers to guide surgery: at each iteration compute an orthonormal $5\times4$ tangent basis for every point once, parametrise displacements by $453\times4$ tangent variables plus $t$, linearise only pairs with slack below $2\times10^{-5}$ (capped at the 2,500 tightest, giving at most eight nonzeros per sparse constraint row), solve with HiGHS under an infinity-norm trust region starting at $10^{-4}$ and adapting by true-max improvement, precompute and reuse the sparse index pattern rather than rebuilding dense $453\times5$ variable matrices, and allow at most about 12 LP solves with a hard 150-second cutoff returning the best-ever configuration. After convergence, inspect the LP duals: keep contacts with positive stress, identify zero-stress contacts and persistent rattlers, then delete or hole-relocate precisely those unconstrained points and repeat once, thereby turning the LP from a slow squeezing device (the mode that previously timed out) into a rigidity/stress diagnostic for targeted topology changes.

idea: Search C151-symmetric codes 453=3x151 in 9 parameters with differential evolution plus LogSumExp refinement, then break symmetry and polish symmetric, hybrid-averaged and incumbent basins with softmax annealing and worst-pair micro-shaving.
direction: Test a hidden low-dimensional symmetric construction suggested by $453=3\times151$: use the cyclic group $C_{151}$ acting on $\mathbb{R}^5=\mathbb{R}^2\oplus\mathbb{R}^2\oplus\mathbb{R}$ by rotation through $2\pi/151$ in the first plane and $2\pi a/151$ in the second plane (try $a\in\{1,10,20,37,50\}$), so that three generic orbits have exactly 151 points each and the whole code is described by only four parameters per orbit representative after fixing the first phase, namely its axial coordinate, split of radius between the two planes, and second-plane phase. Optimise these roughly 12 parameters with `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` or repeated basin hopping using a smooth LogSumExp surrogate for the maximum over the generated 453 points, then take the best symmetric result, break the symmetry, and polish it in the full $453\times5$ space with softmax annealing; even if the symmetric optimum is not itself the record, compare its contact/rattler statistics with the incumbent and use it (or a partially symmetrised incumbent obtained by averaging nearest points onto nearby orbits) as a genuinely different starting basin.

idea: Large delete-and-reinsert basin hops relocating 15/25/40 mixed worst-plus-rattler points into refined large holes with elite archive and sideways acceptance.
direction: Perform large topology-changing delete-and-reinsert basin hops that relocate many points at once: in each cycle remove $k\in\{15,25,40\}$ points chosen as a mixture of the highest-contact-stress/worst points and randomly chosen rattlers, then reinsert them one at a time at approximate largest holes found by scoring 50,000–100,000 random sphere candidates against the retained points, refining each hole by 100–200 steps of single-point softmax descent at $\tau\approx10^{-4}$, and only then re-annealing the full configuration for 300–800 steps. Accept a hop if its polished maximum is within $2\times10^{-4}$ of the incumbent (not only if it immediately improves), keep an elite archive of the best three distinct polished outcomes, restart later hops from different elites, and reserve the final 30 seconds for polishing the overall best; this directly attacks the sparse contact graph by forcing dozens of points to acquire new neighbours simultaneously, which one-point hole moves have failed to do.

Use the rigidity-matrix null space to step along floppy modes and pull the next slack shell into contact, testing retractions at several radii and keeping topology-changing moves for a short polish.
direction: Take a second-order rigidity/null-space step rather than another ordinary LP step. Build tangent bases and the rigidity matrix \(R\) for the approximately \(1{,}700\) contacts at slack \(<10^{-9}\); compute its smallest singular subspace, using randomized SVD or `scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh` on \(RR^{T}\), and parameterize displacements in that null space. Choose a null-space direction that minimizes the predicted second-order increase in contact cosines while driving selected pairs from the next slack shell, \(5\times10^{-7}\) to \(10^{-4}\), toward contact; estimate curvature by trial retractions at several step sizes, accept a step if it either lowers the true maximum or creates a new contact without raising it, and then run a short, time-capped LP polish. Reserve the final 30 seconds for polishing/returning the incumbent so this exploration cannot time out.

idea: Rotate coherent contact-graph caps around overloaded hubs with Cayley-parameterized SO(5) moves to break redundant contacts, then relax with softmax annealing and worst-pair shaving.
direction: Make collective rigid-cluster moves that single-point moves cannot represent. Choose spherical caps or contact-graph communities centred on overloaded hubs, containing roughly \(10\)–\(40\) points, and rotate the whole cluster by a general \(SO(5)\) transformation parameterized by a \(5\times5\) skew-symmetric matrix, optionally combined with a reflection or with rotation about the cap centre. Optimize these at most \(10\) collective parameters with Nelder–Mead or random coordinate search, evaluating only internal and cross-cluster Gram entries for speed; accept promising configurations, counter-rotate or displace neighbouring points, and then apply local softmax followed by LP polishing. Repeat over hubs with different cap radii, because moving a coherent cluster can break several redundant contacts simultaneously while preserving useful internal geometry.

idea: N-changing pressure cycles that delete high-degree hubs (452-pt relaxation + hole reinsertion) and insert extra points (454-pt over-pressure + least-stressed deletion), each with short softmax anneals, keeping only the best two topologies for tiny-radius active-set LP polishing.
direction: Use an \(N\)-changing pressure cycle to force a global topology change. First remove one high-degree hub and globally re-optimize the resulting \(452\)-point code, whose maximum should fall appreciably; then reinsert a point at the largest available spherical hole and jointly re-polish all \(453\) points. In the complementary cycle, insert an additional point at the best hole, optimize the over-pressured \(454\)-point configuration, remove whichever point then has the smallest maximum cosine or least contact stress, and re-polish the remaining \(453\). Try several hub/rattler deletion choices with short softmax anneals, keep only the best two candidates for LP polishing, and always retain the original incumbent unless a cycle produces a verified lower maximum.

idea: Eliminate rattlers and rebalance overloaded hubs with degree-weighted softmax annealing plus targeted hole surgery to reach a uniformly jammed basin.

Frozen-background rattler-plus-hub surgery with sequential 20k+ hole reinsertion and active-set-only softmax plus small LP before a final global polish.
direction: Perform targeted rattler-and-hub surgery with a frozen background. Remove the six rattlers together with six to ten points of highest contact degree or largest dual stress, freeze the remaining points, and reinsert the removed points one at a time at the best of at least \(20{,}000\) sampled spherical holes, scoring each candidate against the frozen and already reinserted points. Then optimize only the reinserted points and their near neighbours—typically a subproblem of under \(100\) tangent variables—using annealed softmax and a small LP, before unfreezing everything for a final global LP polish. Generate several subsets, such as rattlers plus one hub neighbourhood at a time, impose strict per-candidate deadlines, and return the best verified configuration found rather than the last explored one.

idea: Dual-stress backbone plus Jacobian-nullspace floppy-mode surgery with exact-retraction trials and short LP re-polishes to change contact topology.
direction: Dual-stress and floppy-mode surgery using the LP Jacobian nullspace. Build the sparse active-constraint matrix A (pairs with slack <2e-5, tangent coordinates, 10 rotation modes projected out), solve one HiGHS LP and read off dual weights w_ij; identify the positive-stress backbone (w_ij above 1e-6 of the max weight) and the zero-stress contacts. Use scipy.sparse.linalg.svds or randomised SVD to get the ~20 smallest right singular vectors of A, then trial exact retracted moves along each vector and random combinations at amplitudes 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, scoring by exact max cosine plus a penalty for breaking backbone contacts; follow any direction that does not immediately raise the max with a short LP polish (5s cap), since motion along near-null modes is exactly the second-order freedom the LP cannot price and is the cheapest way to change which pairs are tied.

idea: Search R2+R2+R1 cyclic orbit families with multipliers, optimize seeds by differential evolution plus orbit-restricted hill-climb, then break symmetry in Fourier-mode stages with re-polish.
direction: Search group-orbit families properly, with staged symmetry breaking by representation mode rather than random noise. Enumerate block-rotation groups R2+R2+R1 with multipliers (1,a) for orbit partitions summing to 453 beyond 3x151 (e.g. C113 with 4 orbits of 113 plus one fixed pole point, C75, C90/C151 variants with extra pole/equatorial orbits, and the same families with several generic seed orbits), optimise the few seed parameters (each seed modulo its stabiliser) by differential evolution on the exact orbit Gram followed by an orbit-restricted LP polish so the symmetric optimum is reached to <1e-10 before any breaking. Then break symmetry in stages: parametrise tangent perturbations in Fourier modes of the group action, enable the lowest non-trivial mode first with amplitude scanned over 1e-3 to 5e-2, re-polish with LP after each stage, and only then allow full perturbations, retaining the symmetric code itself as a candidate if breaking never beats it.

idea: Break the jammed contact topology with adaptive multi-scale basin-hopping that alternates worst-neighbourhood shakes, overload-degree ejection into sampled large holes, and random-cap rotations, each followed by fast full-matrix softmax tangential momentum annealing plus final worst-pair micro-shaving.
Rattler recruitment by large-hole sampling plus batched LogSumExp tangent refinement and restricted HiGHS LP freeing only moved points and neighbours.
direction: Rattler recruitment to build an isostatic, positively-stressed contact graph. Compute contact degrees at slack 1e-7, freeze all points except the 6 rattlers and points with degree <=2, and for each such point sample 50000 random unit directions, score each by its maximum cosine to the frozen points, keep the 50 candidates in the largest holes, and refine them with tangent-space L-BFGS on a LogSumExp surrogate (tau annealed 1e-3 to 1e-5) until the point sits on the hole boundary with 4-5 near-contacts at the global maximum. Then run the existing HiGHS tangent LP freeing only the moved points plus their 30 nearest neighbours, cycle through all rattlers/low-degree points repeatedly, and accept only moves whose exact max cosine improves; this converts wasted free points into braces that can push down their over-contacted neighbours instead of leaving hubs of degree 14-15 next to free points.

idea: Break the jammed 1700-contact basin with hole-surgery plus Riesz-energy basin-hopping followed by fast RMS-normalized softmax minimax annealing and greedy worst-pair shaving, using no LP so many topology-changing cycles fit in time.
Eject a connected over-braced cluster around a high-degree hub plus a nearby rattler and greedily reinsert points into largest holes followed by restricted neighbourhood LP polish.
direction: Connected-cluster ejection and greedy reinsertion, with a hard internal deadline to avoid the 200s timeouts of previous basin-hopping. Pick a connected cluster in the contact graph consisting of a degree >=12 hub, its contact neighbours, and any nearby rattler (25-40 points total), delete it, and reinsert points one at a time: for each, evaluate 20000 candidate directions against the remaining plus already-reinserted points, take the largest-hole candidate, refine it by local tangent descent, then free only the inserted points and their one-ring contact neighbourhood for a capped LP polish (max 5s per solve, 165s total wall budget, incumbent always kept as fallback). Repeat with several cluster choices and random seeds, accepting a reinsertion sequence only if the final exact max cosine beats 0.8482350832864; this concentrates topological change where the graph is over-braced instead of shaking all 453 points and re-converging to the same jam.

idea: Fast elitist basin-hopping that ejects the worst-contact points into diverse large holes and re-anneals only with vectorized softmax tangential repulsion, avoiding LP timeouts to allow many topology changes.

Use LP dual stress to separate load-bearing backbone contacts from zero-stress contacts and drive topology changes by stepping along the near-nullspace (floppy modes) of the active-constraint Jacobian, then re-polishing with short trust-region LP solves.
direction: Dual-stress and floppy-mode surgery using the LP Jacobian nullspace. Build the sparse active-constraint matrix A (pairs with slack <2e-5, tangent coordinates, 10 rotation modes projected out), solve one HiGHS LP and read off dual weights w_ij; identify the positive-stress backbone (w_ij above 1e-6 of the max weight) and the zero-stress contacts. Use scipy.sparse.linalg.svds or randomised SVD to get the ~20 smallest right singular vectors of A, then trial exact retracted moves along each vector and random combinations at amplitudes 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, scoring by exact max cosine plus a penalty for breaking backbone contacts; follow any direction that does not immediately raise the max with a short LP polish (5s cap), since motion along near-null modes is exactly the second-order freedom the LP cannot price and is the cheapest way to change which pairs are tied.
